rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Awwāb is the repentant worshipper who turns back from sin.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام الأواب التواب المتعبد الراجع عن ذنبه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Imam names piety, diligence, trustworthiness, truthful speech, good companionship, and long prostration among the practices of repentant awwābīn.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال يا با أبا محمد عليكم بالورع والاجتهاد وأداء الأمانة

rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: Abu Basir glosses the awwābīn as people who repeatedly repent.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بصير الأوابون التوابون

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali calls the time after shadows incline and breezes ease the hour of the awwābīn, when needs should be sought from God.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال إذا مالت الأفياء وراحت الأرواح فاطلبوا الحوائج إلى الله

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali Zayn al-Abidin tells a Syrian that the command to give kin their due applies to his own family.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنه أنه قال لرجل من أهل الشام أقرأت القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Spending money in disobedience to God is waste, while spending it for good is moderation.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن الحجاج قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قوله { ولا تبذر تبذيرا }

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Even lawful giving becomes waste when a person gives away all his money and is left with nothing.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عنه عليه السلام في الآية قال بذل الرجل ماله ويقعد ليس له مال

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits Jaʿfar’s gloss that al-maḥsūr means unclothed; another report in this passage uses it for poverty.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي قال قال الصادق عليه السلام المحسور العريان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ajlan reports Jaʿfar giving dates to successive beggars and recounting how the Prophet gave a woman his shirt; God taught measured spending, and al-iḥṣār is poverty.
rows.anchor: فأدبه الله تبارك وتعالى على القصد فقال { ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا }

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar recounts that the Prophet gave away an ounce of gold, then lacked anything for a petitioner; God taught him that giving all one has leaves one destitute.
rows.anchor: قال قال علم الله عز اسمه نبيه كيف ينفق؟ وذلك أنه كانت عنده أوقية من الذهب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Sinan reports that Jaʿfar demonstrated the two expressions by closing his hand and then opening his palm.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك } قال فضم يده

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar defines imlāq as bankruptcy.
rows.anchor: عن إسحاق بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث قال قلت وما الإملاق؟ قال الإفلاس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report says faith leaves the heart during adultery, slander, theft, drinking wine, and embezzlement, but God accepts repentance; the author notes parallel routes and reports that the spirit of faith departs.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة في قوله { ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة } قال قتادة عن الحسن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يقول

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar says excessive retaliation means killing someone other than the killer or mutilating the killer; the heir's authority to take the killer is a great aid.
rows.anchor: نهى أن يقتل غير قاتله أو يمثل بالقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: When two men kill one person, the heir may kill either and the other owes half the blood-price; if a man kills a woman and her heirs insist on execution, they repay half the man's blood-price.
rows.anchor: يخير وليه أن يقتل أيهما شاء ويغرم الباقي نصف الدية أعني دية المقتول

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic retaliation, a tribe might spare its killer and kill a more eminent person instead; the verse admonished this practice.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن الناس في الجاهلية كانوا إذا قتل الرجل من القوم رجلا لم يرضوا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar identifies the just balance as a scale with a tongue; the author says the tongue signifies uprightness, as does a two-pan scale.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام، قال القسطاس المستقيم هو الميزان الذي له لسان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Faith imposes distinct duties on every limb; the eyes must avoid forbidden sights and lower the gaze, a duty tied to accountability for hearing, sight, and heart.
rows.anchor: ففرض على العين أن لا تنظر إلى ما حرم الله عليه وان تغض عما نهاه الله عنه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The legs must not walk toward disobedience but must walk as God commands, including walking without arrogance and with moderation.
rows.anchor: وفرض الله على الرجلين أن لا يمشي بهما إلى شيء من معاصي الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar rebukes a man who listens to neighboring women sing and play the lute, citing accountability for hearing; the man repents and is told to bathe and pray.
rows.anchor: أما سمعت الله يقول { إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا }

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Hearing is questioned about what it hears, sight about what it looks at, and the heart about what it holds.
rows.anchor: قال يسأل السمع عما يسمع والبصر عما يطرف والفؤاد عما يعقد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the prohibition on following what one does not know as forbidding someone to lead another without knowledge.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم } الآية قال قال لا تؤم أحدا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that one who slanders a believing man or woman will be placed in the clay of khabāl or made to answer for the accusation; Jaʿfar's report glosses it as the pus of prostitutes.
rows.anchor: من بهت مؤمنا أو مؤمنة أقيم في طينة خبال أو يخرج مما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports either concern the verse's particular occasion or apply its general rationale, as the preceding explanation indicates.
rows.anchor: والروايات - كما ترى - بعضها مبني على خصوص مورد الآية وبعضها على عموم التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jews suggested three questions to Quraysh as a test of prophethood: the cave companions, Moses and his youth, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: وهي أحد الأمور الثلاثة التي أشار اليهود على قريش أن تسأل النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the Dhul-Qarnayn account, the cave story does not begin with an explicit question formula, though the closing command about tomorrow hints at the question.
rows.anchor: غير أن هذه القصة لم تصدر بما يدل على تعلق السؤال بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening verses imply that the cave story was already generally known before revelation, while revelation supplies its details beginning with the truthful account.
rows.anchor: وسياق الآيات الثلاث التي افتتحت بها القصة مشعر بأن قصة الكهف كانت معلومة إجمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave sleepers mirror humanity absorbed in earthly adornment: people will awaken from worldly life and reckon its long span as a day or part of one.
rows.anchor: ليس ذلك كله إلا آية إلهية هي نظيرة ما جرى على أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave story answers the Prophet's grief over unbelief by showing that worldly distraction is itself a recurring sign like the sleepers' awakening.
rows.anchor: بل حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف كانوا من آياتنا بدعا عجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is left implicit to preserve the Prophet's standing; the indirect allusion is more forceful than an explicit statement.
rows.anchor: ولأن الكناية أبلغ من التصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave companions and people of the inscription are one group; their names reflect entering the cave and the story recorded about them.
rows.anchor: أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم جماعة بأعيانهم والقصة قصتهم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others explain al-Raqīm as an inscribed tablet or royal record, the mountain, valley, town, or dog associated with the story.
rows.anchor: قيل إن قصتهم كانت منقوشة في لوح منصوب هناك أو محفوظ في خزانة الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the Raqīm people were a separate group is far-fetched: the passage would not detail one story while leaving the other wholly unmentioned, and their reported story clashes with context.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن أصحاب الرقيم غير أصحاب الكهف وقصتهم غير قصتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kahf is a mountain cavern, wider than a cave; a smaller one is called a ghār.
rows.anchor: والكهف هو المغارة في الجبل إلا أنه أوسع منها فإذا صغر سمي غارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raqīm derives from writing and is originally a passive participle, like al-jarīḥ and al-qatīl.
rows.anchor: والرقيم من الرقم وهو الكتابة والخط فهو في الأصل فعيل بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjab is a verbal noun used adjectivally to intensify the sense of wonder.
rows.anchor: والعجب مصدر بمعنى التعجب أريد به معنى الوصف مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitya is a collective plural of fatā, meaning a young man, with a shade of praise.
rows.anchor: والفتية جمع سماعي لفتى والفتى الشاب ولا تخلو الكلمة من شائبة مدح

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī says preparation originally means bringing a thing into a formed state.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي وأصل التهيئة إحداث هيأة الشيء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines rushd as guidance to the desired end, the opposite of error, and says it is used like guidance.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الرشد والرشد خلاف الغي يستعمل استعمال الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal for mercy follows their helpless arrival; asking it from God specifically shows exhausted means and desperation.
rows.anchor: تفريع لدعائهم على أويهم كأنهم اضطروا لفقد القوة وانقطاع الحيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested mercy may mean divine support, since no one else can support them; alternatively it may mean gifts reserved to God, especially guidance, as in the prayer of the firmly grounded.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالرحمة المسؤولة التأييد الإلهي إذ لا مؤيد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their affair is their perilous situation after fleeing persecutors who kill believers and force them to worship other than God; rushd means finding a path to safety.
rows.anchor: والتجأوا إلى كهف وهم لا يدرون ماذا سيجري عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mercy means divine support, the guidance clause explains it; if it means a specific gift, the clause adds a separate request.
rows.anchor: على أول الاحتمالين السابقين في معنى الرحمة عطف تفسير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads striking their ears as placing a barrier that made them sleep so deeply that sounds could not wake them.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف أي ضربنا عليها حجابا من أن تسمع يعني أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains striking their ears as God imposing sleep; the author finds this more eloquent than al-Zamakhsharī's account.
rows.anchor: وقال في المجمع ومعنى ضربنا على آذانهم سلطنا عليهم النوم، وهو من الكلام البالغ في الفصاحة

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub compares the expression to an Arab idiom for an emir striking someone's hand, meaning he prevents that person from acting.
rows.anchor: قال قطرب هو كقول العرب ضرب الأمير على يد فلان إذا منعه من التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the meaning reported by al-Majmaʿ is more eloquent than al-Zamakhshari's paraphrase.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره من المعنى أبلغ مما ذكره الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is among the Quran's eloquent expressions and cannot be translated with a meaning that matches its phrasing.
rows.anchor: وقال هذا من فصيح لغات القرآن التي لا يمكن أن يترجم بمعنى يوافق اللفظ

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ḥizb as a substantial group.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب الحزب جماعة فيها غلظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may also allude to a mother's gentle tapping near a child's ear to lull it, making their sleep resemble tender maternal care.
rows.anchor: وهنا معنى ثالث وإن لم يذكروه وهو أن يكون إشارة إلى ما تصنعه النساء عند إنامة الصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanin is an adverbial accusative, and ʿadad is a verbal noun meaning counted years; alternatively, a genitive complement is elided, yielding years possessing a number.
rows.anchor: والعدد مصدر كالعد بمعنى المعدود فالمعنى سنين معدودة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says counted years can suggest abundance or scarcity, since a long span is small in God's reckoning.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف إن توصيف السنين بالعدد يحتمل أن يراد به التكثير أو التقليل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a small quantity is already easy to grasp without counting, while a large quantity needs to be counted.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج إن الشيء إذا قل فهم مقدار عدده فلم يحتج أن يعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that counted signals a small, easily numbered span, fitting the passage's denial that the story is uniquely astonishing; the sleepers were not dead.
rows.anchor: وكون الغرض من التوصيف بالعدد هو التقليل هو الملائم للسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿth here means waking them, not resurrection, because the preceding verse describes sleep.
rows.anchor: المراد بالبعث هو الايقاظ دون الاحياء بقرينة الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amad is a duration with an unknown but bounded endpoint, while abad is unlimited; amad focuses on an endpoint whereas zamān can span beginning and end.
rows.anchor: الأمد والأبد يتقاربان لكن الأبد عبارة عن مدة الزمان التي ليس لها حد محدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amad differs from zamān by considering a duration's endpoint, while zamān can encompass both its beginning and endpoint.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الأمد والزمان أن الأمد يقال باعتبار الغاية والزمان عام في المبدأ والغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge here is actual manifestation of an event in its particular existence.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعلم، العلم الفعلي وهو ظهور الشيء وحضوره بوجوده الخاص عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses knowledge in the sense of actual manifestation, as in the verses about knowing who supports God and that the messengers delivered their messages.
rows.anchor: ليعلم الله من ينصره ورسله بالغيب الحديد 25، وقوله ليعلم أن قد أبلغوا رسالات ربهم الجن 28

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters gloss the phrase as making what God already knows manifest.
rows.anchor: وإليه يرجع قول بعضهم في تفسيره أن المعنى ليظهر معلومنا على ما علمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause gives the purpose for awakening them, with the lam marking an intended end.
rows.anchor: تعليل للبعث واللام للغاية والمراد بالحزبين الطائفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two factions are the cave youths questioning one another after awakening; identifying them instead as believers and unbelievers among their people is remote.
rows.anchor: المراد بالحزبين الطائفتان من أصحاب الكهف حين سأل بعضهم بعضا بعد البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥṣā is most naturally a past-tense verb, with amad as its object and the phrase about their stay restricting the duration counted.
rows.anchor: وما مصدرية أي أي الحزبين عد أمد لبثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading aḥṣā as a comparative adjective and supplying an implied verb for amad is possible but strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل أحصى اسم تفضيل من الإحصاء بحذف الزوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three verses summarize their flight and prayer for rescue, their counted years of sleep, and their awakening to determine which faction counted the duration.
rows.anchor: إذ رجع الشبان إلى الكهف فسألوا عند ذلك ربهم قائلين ربنا هب لنا من لدنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each opening verse gives one of the story's three summary elements; later verses add what happened after the people discovered them.
rows.anchor: فلإجمال القصة أركان ثلاثة تتضمن كل واحدة من الآيات الثلاث واحدا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faith was pleasing to God, since otherwise God would not have ascribed it to them.
rows.anchor: آمنوا إيمانا مرضيا لربهم ولولا ذلك لم ينسبه إليهم قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their increased guidance means that faith rose toward what leads to God's pleasure, as also described in 57:28.
rows.anchor: الهدى بعد أصل الإيمان ملازم لارتقاء درجة الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabt means binding; strengthening hearts is a metaphor for removing their anxiety and agitation. Shataṭ is exceeding truth, and sulṭān is proof.
rows.anchor: الربط هو الشد، والربط على القلوب كناية عن سلب القلق والاضطراب عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses recount the youths' first public argument against paganism, targeting the supposed divinity of angels, jinn, and revered humans rather than the idols that merely depict them.
rows.anchor: وقد أتوا بكلام مملوء حكمة وفهما راموا به إبطال ربوبية أرباب الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational pronoun in the command to bring proof against the claimed gods supports the reading that the argument targets rational beings.
rows.anchor: ومن الشاهد على ذلك قوله { عليهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They affirm one Lord of heaven and earth against paganism's separate deity for each created kind, then deny all other gods, including the higher beings claimed by some traditions.
rows.anchor: فبدأوا بإثبات توحيده بقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling any creature divine exceeds proper bounds by elevating it to the Creator's rank.
rows.anchor: فدلوا على أن دعوة غيره من التجاوز عن الحد بالغلو في حق المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand for clear proof answers the polytheists' appeal that God is too exalted to perceive directly: all creatures know God through His names, attributes, and effects according to capacity.
rows.anchor: والجميع منا ومنهم يعرفونه بأسمائه وصفاته وآثاره كل على قدر طاقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation, provision, ownership, and governance belong to God alone, so only He possesses the attributes that merit worship.
rows.anchor: أن جميع الصفات الموجبة لاستحقاق العبادة من الخلق والرزق والملك والتدبير له وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without decisive proof, their claim is speech about God without knowledge and a lie against Him, the greatest injustice; this shows the youths' insight and confirms their increased guidance.
rows.anchor: فلو لم يقيموه كان قولهم من القول بغير علم في الله وهو افتراء الكذب عليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies they spoke openly amid coercive idol worship, not in private; denying gods after affirming God's lordship hints that they were compelled to invoke idols.
rows.anchor: فيه إشعار وتلويح إلى أنه كان هناك تكليف إجباري بعبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They most likely rose during an assembly enforcing idol worship, publicly declared monotheism, and fled under mortal threat; a report that six were the king's advisers supports this.
rows.anchor: الأظهر هو الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public confession does not conflict with reports that they had concealed their faith: they could have practiced caution before suddenly declaring belief and leaving.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي ذلك ما سيأتي من الروايات أنهم كانوا يسرون إيمانهم ويعملون بالتقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings take their standing as rising for God, or place the speeches after they left town; on these readings their strengthened hearts meant they feared no consequence of flight.
rows.anchor: وربما احتمل أن يكون المراد بقيامهم قيامهم لله نصرة منهم للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtizāl is withdrawal, nashr is spreading, and mirfaq, with the cited vowelings, means gentle treatment or kind benefit.
rows.anchor: الاعتزال والتعزل التنحي عن أمر، والنشر البسط، والمرفق بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء وبالعكس وبفتحهما المعاملة بلطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After leaving the people and their gods, they advise hiding in the cave, confident God will extend mercy and provide ease; these are the same gifts they requested on entering.
rows.anchor: وهذان اللذان تفرسوا بهما من نشر الرحمة وتهيئة المرفق هما اللذان سألوهما بعد دخول الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception in “what they worship except God” is disconnected: the passage does not imply idolaters worshipped God alongside idols, contrary to other interpretations.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله { وما يعبدون إلا الله } استثناء منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazāwur means leaning aside, taqriḍ means cutting across, fujwah is a broad open space, and right and left may denote their respective directions.
rows.anchor: والفجوة المتسع من الأرض وساحة الدار والمراد بذات اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage depicts the cave and sleepers' position; the address is to the Prophet as a hearer and, by extension, to any observer.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بما أنه سامع لا بما أنه هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's rays reach the sides of the cave at sunrise and sunset while the youths lie in a spacious interior that the sun does not strike.
rows.anchor: وهم في متسع من الكهف لا تناله الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author infers a pole-facing entrance, with sunlight falling along one inner side at each time but not on the sleepers, protecting their bodies, clothing, and comfort.
rows.anchor: ولا يقع عليهم لأنهم كانوا في متسع منه فوقاهم الله بذلك من أن يؤذيهم حر الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators place the entrance toward the north pole and locate the cave at Ephesus, with right and left judged from inside.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر المفسرون أن الكهف كان بابه مقابلا للقطب الشمالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a house or cave with a doorway, right and left are reckoned from outside facing in; by that convention the cave would face south, contrary to the commentators' north-facing account.
rows.anchor: والمعمول في اعتبار اليمين واليسار لمثل الكهف والبيت والفسطاط وكل ما له باب أن يؤخذ باعتبار الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the cave's orientation, its arrangement is divine care that preserved them until their appointed term.
rows.anchor: وعلى أي حال كان وضعهم هذا من عناية الله ولطفه بهم ليستبقيهم بذلك حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aiqāẓ means awake people and ruqūd sleepers; the phrasing hints that they slept with eyes open.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام تلويح إلى أنهم كانوا مفتوحي الأعين حال نومهم كالأيقاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned them from side to side to prevent decay of their bodies and clothes and loss of bodily strength from prolonged stillness.
rows.anchor: والمراد نقلبهم تارة من اليمين إلى الشمال وتارة من الشمال إلى اليمين لئلا تأكلهم الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waṣīd is the courtyard or threshold; the dog lay at the cave entrance and remained with them throughout their stay.
rows.anchor: الوصيد فناء البيت وقيل عتبة الدار والمعنى كانوا على ما وصف من الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appearance was so frightening that an observer would flee in anticipation of harm and be filled with dread spreading through the body.
rows.anchor: بيان أنهم وحالهم هذا الحال كان لهم منظر موحش هائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasāʾul is mutual questioning; waraq is dirhams or silver, coined or uncoined; yuẓhirū ʿalaykum can mean discover or overcome you.
rows.anchor: التساؤل سؤال بعض القوم بعضا، والورق بالفتح فالكسر الدراهم، وقيل هو الفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise We awakened them” refers back to their long, remarkable sleep; the questioning was the immediate purpose of waking them.
rows.anchor: كما أنمناهم في الكهف دهرا طويلا على هذا الوضع العجيب المدهش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their despair at the apparent triumph of coercive falsehood parallels the man revived after a century; their awakening shows that time's length does not destroy truth or revive falsehood.
rows.anchor: فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earthly life and its events pass like a brief dream, but worldly distraction keeps people from recognizing the truth until death or the end of the world.
rows.anchor: وجدها كطائف في نومة أو سنة في مثل يوم

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali says people are asleep and awaken when they die.
rows.anchor: الناس نيام فإذا ماتوا انتبهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity will also awaken when the world's adornment is folded up and the human world is brought to extinction.
rows.anchor: ويوم آخر وهو يوم يطوى فيه بساط الدنيا وزينتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioning is the real purpose of awakening and aligns with the purpose stated in 18:12.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { ليتساءلوا بينهم } غاية لبعثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating the questioning as only a subordinate purpose lacks textual evidence; treating it as a mere consequence does not answer the objection that it is a small outcome of a great miracle.
rows.anchor: وهذا مع عدم شاهد عليه من جهة اللفظ تكلف ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One youth asked the others how long they had slept, apparently sensing a long interval from the heaviness of their sleep.
rows.anchor: وكأن السائل استشعر طولا في لبثهم مما وجده من لوثة النوم الثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A day or part of a day” is one speaker's uncertain estimate based on the sun's changed position, not a division in which some said a day and others part of one.
rows.anchor: وقد أجاب بمثله شخص واحد بعينه قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observed sun, shadows, light, and darkness cannot establish an exact full day; here “day” commonly means slightly more than a night and day.
rows.anchor: الأمور الخارجية التي يستدل بها الإنسان وخاصة من نام ثم انتبه من شمس وظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “your Lord knows” states an epistemic truth: humans know external events only through indicators, while God alone directly encompasses each thing and event.
rows.anchor: فإن الإنسان محجوب عما وراء نفسه لا يملك بإذن الله إلا نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers who appeal to God's knowledge show higher monotheistic insight than those who estimate a day; they are a different group, not the factions in 18:12.
rows.anchor: أن القائلين منهم { ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم } كانوا أعلى كعبا في مقام المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue implies at least seven youths: one asks, and each of two plural replies requires at least three people.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يستفاد أن القوم كانوا سبعة أو أزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They propose sending one of their own to buy food; “which one” refers grammatically to the city but means its residents.
rows.anchor: الضمير في { أيها } راجع إلى المدينة والمراد بها أهلها من الكسبة استخداما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested errand is to obtain food for them to eat, introduced as a proposal to the group.
rows.anchor: وفيه أمر أو عرض لهم أن يرسلوا رسولا منهم إلى المدينة ليشتري لهم طعاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakiy food may mean good, lawful, or pure food; the comparative form favors the first sense.
rows.anchor: وزكاء الطعام كونه طيبا وقيل كونه حلالا وقيل كونه طاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “bring you sustenance from it,” the pronoun most naturally refers to the food; taking it to refer to the silver is remote and requires an extra implied pronoun.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { منه } للطعام المفهوم من الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talaṭṭuf is acting gently and showing care; in context the envoy should deal smoothly with residents to avoid a quarrel that reveals them.
rows.anchor: والمراد على ما يعطيه السياق ليتكلف اللطف مع أهل المدينة في ذهابه ومجيئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader reading of tact as general caution in transactions is not supported by the explicit following clause.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى ليتكلف اللطف في المعاملة وإطلاق الكلام يدفعه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib traces ẓuhūr to visibility, from which the word extends to learning of something, finding it, or prevailing over it.
rows.anchor: والكلمة على ما ذكره الراغب مأخوذة من الظهر بمعنى الجارحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers “discover your location” for yuẓhirū ʿalaykum because it covers how the powerful townspeople could then capture and overpower the youths.
rows.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن يكون { يظهروا عليكم } بمعنى يطلعوا عليكم ويعلموا بمكانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of stoning signals the townspeople's hostility to the youths' faith and the likelihood of a collective attack.
rows.anchor: وفي اختيار الرجم على غيره من أصناف القتل إشعار بأن أهل المدينة عامة كانوا يعادونهم لدينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return you into their creed” uses a verb carrying the sense of insertion, hence the preposition fi rather than ilā.
rows.anchor: الإعادة مضمن معنى الإدخال ولذا عدي بفي دون إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being returned would likely mean enforced participation in idol worship and loss of their true religious practices, not only verbal assent.
rows.anchor: أن لا يقنع القوم بمجرد اعترافهم بحقية الملة صورة دون أن يثقوا بصدقهم في الاعتراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A captive or weak person trapped in an unbelieving society may comply under coercion while keeping faith inwardly, as 16:106 and 3:28 allow.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone free to leave who voluntarily enters a hostile society and loses the ability to profess faith has wronged himself; 4:97 rebukes those who claim they were helpless despite a spacious earth.
rows.anchor: وأما من كان بنجوة منهم وهو حر في اعتقاده وعمله ثم ألقى بنفسه في مهلكة الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects proposed harmonizations: coerced apostasy leading to Satanic influence, return by invitation alone, or a period when dissimulation was forbidden lack textual support.
rows.anchor: وقد أجابوا عن الإشكال بوجوه أخر غير مقنعة منها أن الإكراه على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exchange portrays close fellowship: they share religious insight, delegate equally, use communal money, advise tact, and care for one another's safety.
rows.anchor: وسياق ما حكي من محاورتهم أعني قوله { لبثتم } إلى تمام الآيتين سياق عجيب دال على كمال تحابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic phrase “your silver, this” is unusual for a food errand; the coin's age—three centuries—caused the youths to be recognized.
rows.anchor: ولعلها إنما ذكرت في الآية مع خصوصية الإشارة لأنها كانت هي السبب لظهور أمرهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿathara literally means to stumble and figuratively to learn of something without seeking it; thus God caused people to discover the youths.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات عثر الرجل يعثر عثرا وعثورا إذا سقط ويتجوز به فيمن يطلع على أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with their awakening, God caused people to discover them; the implied object is the people, and the promise made clear to them is resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي وكما أنساهم دهرا ثم بعثناهم لكذا وكذا كذلك أعثرنا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Hour has no doubt” explains the promise of God; the people are disputing resurrection, and the dispute's wording signals their concern for it.
rows.anchor: ويكون قوله { وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها } عطفا تفسيريا لسابقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discovery either occurs while people debate resurrection so they learn the promise is true, or is timed to that debate so they learn it then.
rows.anchor: أطلعنا الناس عليهم في زمان يتنازعون أي الناس بينهم في أمر البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sleep and awakening parallel death and resurrection: sensation and bodily functions ceased for centuries, yet bodies and clothing remained intact before they returned to their former state.
rows.anchor: وسلامة ظاهر أبدانهم وثيابهم عن الدثور والبلى ثم رجوعهم إلى حالهم يوم دخلوا الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the cave episode and bodily resurrection are extraordinary events; denying them rests on bare incredulity rather than evidence.
rows.anchor: وهما معا من خوارق العادة لا يدفعهما إلا الاستبعاد من غير دليل
